user_text: Plan a 1-day migration from SVN to Git for a small repo.
assistant_text:
# 1-Day SVN to Git Migration Plan

## Pre-Migration Checklist (Night Before)

- [ ] Notify all team members — **freeze SVN commits** during migration
- [ ] Confirm you have admin access to both SVN and new Git host (GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket)
- [ ] Back up the SVN repository

```bash
# Backup SVN repo
svnadmin dump /path/to/svn/repo > svn_backup.dump
```

---

## Morning: Preparation (8:00–10:00 AM)

### 1. Install Prerequisites
```bash
# macOS
brew install git git-svn svn

# Ubuntu/Debian
sudo apt install git git-svn subversion
```

### 2. Build Authors File
Map SVN usernames → Git identities (required for commit history).

```bash
# Extract all SVN authors automatically
svn log svn://your-repo-url --quiet \
  | grep "^r" \
  | awk '{print $3}' \
  | sort -u > authors.txt
```

Edit `authors.txt` into this format:
```
jsmith = John Smith <john.smith@company.com>
mjones = Mary Jones <mary.jones@company.com>
(no author) = Legacy User <legacy@company.com>
```

### 3. Create the Git Repository on Your Host
- Create a **new empty repo** on GitHub/GitLab (no README, no .gitignore)
- Copy the remote URL for later

---

## Mid-Morning: Clone SVN → Git (10:00 AM–12:00 PM)

### Standard Layout (trunk/branches/tags)
```bash
git svn clone svn://your-repo-url \
  --stdlayout \
  --authors-file=authors.txt \
  --no-metadata \
  -A authors.txt \
  my-git-repo
```

### Non-Standard Layout (no branches/tags)
```bash
git svn clone svn://your-repo-url \
  --authors-file=authors.txt \
  --no-metadata \
  my-git-repo
```

> ⏱️ **Time varies** — small repos usually finish in minutes. Grab coffee.

---

## Midday: Clean Up the Repo (12:00–1:00 PM)

```bash
cd my-git-repo
```

### Convert SVN Branches → Git Branches
```bash
# List remote SVN branches
git branch -r

# Convert each branch
git checkout -b feature-x refs/remotes/feature-x
```

### Convert SVN Tags → Git Tags
```bash
# Convert all SVN tags to proper Git tags
for tag in $(git branch -r | grep "tags/" | sed 's/.*tags\///'); do
  git tag "$tag" "refs/remotes/tags/$tag"
  git branch -r -d "tags/$tag"
done
```

### Add a .gitignore
```bash
# Convert SVN ignores to .gitignore
git svn show-ignore > .gitignore
git add .gitignore
git commit -m "chore: add .gitignore from SVN properties"
```

### Remove SVN Tracking Refs
```bash
git branch -r | grep -v HEAD | xargs -I{} git branch -rd {}
```

---

## Afternoon: Verify & Push (1:00–3:00 PM)

### Verify History
```bash
# Check commit count matches SVN
git log --oneline | wc -l

# Spot-check commits
git log --oneline -20

# Check branches and tags
git branch -a
git tag -l
```

### Push to Remote
```bash
git remote add origin https://github.com/your-org/your-repo.git

# Push main branch
git push -u origin main

# Push all branches
git push origin --all

# Push all tags
git push origin --tags
```

---

## Late Afternoon: Team Onboarding (3:00–5:00 PM)

### Each Developer Runs
```bash
# Clone the new repo
git clone https://github.com/your-org/your-repo.git

# Verify history is intact
git log --oneline
```

### Update These Immediately
| Item | Action |
|------|--------|
| CI/CD pipelines | Point to new Git repo URL |
| Issue tracker | Update repo links |
| README/docs | Update clone instructions |
| Webhooks | Reconfigure for Git events |
| SVN repo | Set to **read-only** (don't delete yet) |

---

## End of Day: Sign-Off Checklist

- [ ] All branches migrated
- [ ] All tags migrated
- [ ] Full commit history preserved
- [ ] `.gitignore` in place
- [ ] CI/CD pipeline passing on new repo
- [ ] Team successfully cloned and can push
- [ ] SVN repo set to read-only
- [ ] Migration documented in team wiki

---

## Rollback Plan
> If something goes wrong, SVN is still intact and read-only.

```bash
# Re-enable SVN writes if needed
# Simply revert the read-only setting on your SVN server
# No data was deleted during this process
```

---

## Quick Reference: Common Issues

| Problem | Fix |
|---------|-----|
| Unknown author error | Add missing user to `authors.txt` and re-run |
| Empty branches | Check `git branch -r` for remote refs |
| Large repo taking too long | Use `--revision HEAD:1` to clone in reverse |
| Tags showing as branches | Re-run the tag conversion loop above |

---

**Total estimated time: 6–8 hours** for a small repo with a small team. The clone step is the longest — everything else is configuration. 🚀

Based on the migration plan above, the top 3 risks are:

---

## Top 3 Migration Risks

### 1. 🕓 Incomplete or Corrupted Commit History
**What can go wrong:** Missing authors in `authors.txt` will cause `git svn clone` to **abort mid-clone**, and SVN externals, binary files, or merge tracking metadata may not translate cleanly to Git.

**Mitigation:**
- Extract and verify the authors file **completely** before cloning
- Audit commit counts and spot-check key commits after migration
- Keep the SVN backup (`svn_backup.dump`) until fully verified

---

### 2. 🔀 Branches and Tags Not Migrating Correctly
**What can go wrong:** SVN branches and tags are just folders by convention — `git svn` may import them as **remote tracking refs instead of real Git branches/tags**, or miss them entirely if the repo uses a non-standard layout.

**Mitigation:**
- Run `git branch -r` after cloning to audit every remote ref
- Manually verify the tag conversion loop worked with `git tag -l`
- Test checkout of each branch before pushing to remote

---

### 3. 🚨 Team Continues Committing to SVN During Migration
**What can go wrong:** If the SVN freeze isn't enforced, commits made during migration will be **permanently lost** — they won't exist in Git and the SVN repo will be retired.

**Mitigation:**
- Communicate the freeze window clearly the day before
- **Set SVN to read-only** at the start of migration, not the end
- Schedule during low-activity hours (early morning or Friday evening)

---

> **Biggest single risk:** #3 — it's the only one that causes **unrecoverable data loss** if the SVN backup is also discarded too early.

## Migration Risk Checklist

### 1. 🕓 Commit History
- [ ] All SVN authors mapped in `authors.txt` before cloning
- [ ] Commit count matches between SVN and Git
- [ ] Key commits spot-checked after migration

### 2. 🔀 Branches & Tags
- [ ] All branches verified with `git branch -r` post-clone
- [ ] All tags verified with `git tag -l` post-conversion
- [ ] Each branch successfully checked out before push

### 3. 🚨 SVN Freeze
- [ ] Team notified of freeze window day before
- [ ] SVN set to **read-only at migration start**
- [ ] SVN backup retained until Git repo fully verified

If the migration fails at any point, **re-enable write access to the SVN repository.**

> The original SVN repo is untouched throughout the entire migration process — it is the single source of truth until the Git repo is fully verified and signed off.

**An authors file mapping every SVN username to a Git identity.**

> Without this, `git svn clone` will abort mid-migration when it encounters an unknown author.

user_text: What is the fastest validation step?
assistant_text:
**Compare commit counts between SVN and Git.**

```bash
# SVN count
svn log svn://your-repo-url --quiet | grep "^r" | wc -l

# Git count
git log --oneline | wc -l
```

> Takes seconds to run and immediately confirms whether history was fully transferred.
**Prep (8–10AM) → Clone (10AM–12PM) → Clean up (12–1PM) → Verify & Push (1–3PM) → Team onboarding (3–5PM)**

user_text: Provide two tools you might use.
assistant_text:
1. **`git svn`** — clones the SVN repository and converts history to Git commits
2. **`svnadmin`** — backs up the SVN repository before migration begins

user_text: State who should approve the final cutover.
assistant_text: **The team lead or repository owner** — they are accountable for confirming that history, branches, tags, and CI/CD pipelines are verified before SVN is set permanently to read-only.
**Send a single clear message to the whole team the day before, stating the exact freeze start time, expected cutover time, and who to contact if something goes wrong.**

## Final Recap

| # | Phase | Key Action |
|---|-------|------------|
| 1 | **Prep** | Map all SVN authors, back up repo, freeze commits |
| 2 | **Clone** | Run `git svn clone` with authors file |
| 3 | **Clean Up** | Convert branches, tags, and add `.gitignore` |
| 4 | **Verify** | Compare commit counts, check branches and tags |
| 5 | **Push** | Push all branches and tags to remote |
| 6 | **Onboard** | Team clones Git repo, CI/CD updated |
| 7 | **Sign Off** | Team lead approves, SVN set to read-only |

> **One rule:** Don't retire the SVN backup until the Git repo is fully verified, the team is onboarded, and the team lead has signed off. Everything else is recoverable — discarding the backup too early is not.

- Map authors before cloning
- Freeze SVN at migration start
- Clone with `git svn`
- Convert branches and tags
- Compare commit counts
- Push all branches and tags
- Update CI/CD pipelines
- Team lead approves cutover
- Set SVN to read-only
- Keep backup until fully verified
